subject: Private inference — control plane routing & air-gapped PoC recap and next tests
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private inference — control plane routing & air-gapped PoC recap and next tests

Hi Jared — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next tests so we stay aligned.

Recap of what we heard from EdgeRetail:
- Goal: run payment-fraud model inference for offline checkout kiosks with strict data residency and no egress from retail DMZ.
- Constraints: air-gapped sites for some stores, corporate VPC with Transit Gateway for others; on-prem firewalls only allow outbound TLS to whitelisted IPs.
- Must minimize latency for per-request inference (<120ms p99 if possible) and keep audit logs retained for 12 months.

Redwood differentiators (short):
- Private control plane option that accepts only egress (outbound) connections + mTLS; no inbound hole in your DMZ.
- Local worker nodes that perform inference behind your network (VPC / on-prem) with KV cache and batching to preserve throughput.
- Automatic fallback routing to hosted inference in a different region only when explicitly allowed by routing policy.

Requested items from your side to scope the PoC:
1) VPC/Network diagram (Transit GW / NAT / firewall rules) — helps us design allowed IP ranges and route preferences.
2) Representative latency window and RPS (e.g., 50 concurrent kiosks, avg 1 req/s).
3) Any strict egress-only policy language from your security team.

Proposed next tests (minimal disruptive sequence):
A) Network reachability test: We provide an outbound proxy endpoint and a small connectivity script that your infra team runs (test verifies mTLS handshake and IP allowlisting).
B) Local worker smoke run: deploy a single Redwood worker VM in a staging VPC that has no inbound access; run 1000 inference requests across 1 hour to capture p50/p95/p99 token latencies and throughput characteristics.
C) Air-gapped feasibility check: for one pilot store we’ll attempt a completely offline worker image (no control-plane egress) and validate that model weights + runtime boot is possible in your air-gapped environment. This is the higher-effort item and we’ll only attempt it after A+B succeed.

Attachments I’m including: redwood_controlplane_options.pdf (short options matrix) and network_requirements.xlsx (checklist + ports/IPs).

Proposed owners & timeline:
- Rishi: overall PoC coordination + infra questions
- Marissa: PoC test plan & data handling/security checklist
- EdgeRetail infra: provide diagram + run connectivity script

Can you confirm availability to run test A next week (suggest Tue/Wed window)? If OK I’ll schedule the kickoff and open a SUP ticket for tracking.

Thanks —
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Rishi, thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with what we need. A few clarifications and a diagram attached.

Answers:
- Representative load: pilot will be ~60 kiosks, bursty during peak; target steady-state 60 rps (worst-case), average 15 rps.
- Latency target: p95 < 150ms acceptable for pilot; we’ll want to tighten later.
- Security: our policy allows outbound TLS to whitelisted IPs only; no persistent inbound ports.

Attachment: edgeretail_vpc_diagram.pdf — shows Transit Gateway, NAT instances, and per-store VPNs (pilot store #22 is air-gapped today).

We can run test A on Wednesday 2026-07-14 between 09:00-12:00 PT. I’ll loop in our infra lead if needed for the runbook.

Thanks —
Jared Lin
Director of Infrastructure, EdgeRetail
jared@edgeretail.com

Thanks, Rishi & Jared — adding a technical checklist and suggested PoC test steps from our side. I attached a short PoC test plan (poc-test-plan.md). Highlights:

1) Network reachability (test A)
- We’ll provide a short Python script and a temporary outbound-only endpoint with mTLS certs. Expected outputs: TLS handshake success, mutual auth logs.

2) Worker smoke run (test B)
- Image contains runtime + model shard (we’ll use a small quantized model for pilot).
- Metrics to capture: token latency, CPU/GPU utilization, socket churn, KV cache hit rate.
- We’ll instrument with Prometheus/OTEL and share a temp dashboard.

3) Air-gap boot (test C) — feasibility checklist
- We need a way to stage model artifacts & runtime via removable media (s3 export -> signed image).
- Confirming: if store #22 allows one-time manual image install and no control-plane egress, we can verify local-only inference for baseline. This will not support model updates without a physical process.

Data & compliance notes:
- We'll ensure audit logs are delivered to your SIEM via secure push or syslog; retention configurable.
- For SOC 2 evidence, please share the specific control objectives you need; we’ll collect the mapping.

If Wed 07/14 works for test A, we’ll prep the script and send the cert pair by EOD Monday.

Marissa
